newsitem.title: QATAR: Elf says oil field in Qatar to pump soon.
newsitem.headline: Elf says oil field in Qatar to pump soon.

text.p: Elf Petroleum Qatar, a unit of Elf Aquitaine, on Monday said it will start oil production at Qatar's offshore al-Khaleej field soon.
"Production will start at 20,000 barrels per day (bpd), rising gradually to 30,000 (bpd) by the year end", said a company official.
"We are preparing to put the field on stream anytime soon", added the official.
The field in the eastern part of Qatar's offshore area was discovered by Elf in 1990. But financial and technical hurdles delayed production.
Elf has a 25-year production-sharing agreement with state Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) to develop the field.
Elf is operator, with Italy's Agip SpA holding a 45 percent share.
The field was due to go on stream in January.
But production was halted due to a leak in a 12-inch pipeline linking the production facilities in the field to Halul island -- Qatar's offshore oil export terminal.
The company official said the leak has been repaired.
Khaleej is one of the seven fields awarded by Qatar to foreign companies under production sharing agreements to boost the oil production capacity to more than 700,000 bpd by the year 2001.
Improved technology and new fields going on stream have enabled Qatar to raise production capacity so far to 500,000 bpd from less than 400,000 bpd two years ago.
The U.S. firm Atlantic Richfield Co began producing 25,000 bpd last summer. Pennzoil Co and Chevron Corp have just started exploration and drilling.
